title: Implementation and Validation of Non-invasive Hemoglobin Screening as an Index Test to Optimize Anemia Diagnostic in children in different clinical settings (normal ward, neonatal, oncologic, perioperative, intensive care)
summary:
In children, the amount of the red blood pigment that carries oxygen is usually measured using a blood sample. If its level is too low, the child has anaemia. Repeated blood sampling can be burdensome, particularly for very small or seriously ill children.

This study investigates whether a light sensor placed on a finger or toe can reliably indicate anaemia. The sensor reading is compared with a blood test that is already needed for the child's clinical care. No additional blood is taken for the study.

Children and adolescents aged under 18 years can participate before surgery, during cancer treatment, or while receiving care in a neonatal or paediatric intensive care unit. The sensor is applied twice in succession. Some children may undergo further measurements during their clinical care.

The analysis takes the child's age and clinical situation into account. The aim is to determine whether some blood tests could be avoided in the future without missing clinically important low levels of the red blood pigment. During the study, treatment remains unchanged and decisions continue to be based on the usual clinical assessments.

interventions.name:
Children and adolescents aged under 18 years with a clinically indicated haemoglobin measurement are prospectively enrolled at the University Medical Center Mainz. Recruitment takes place in perioperative care, neonatology, neonatal and paediatric intensive care, and paediatric oncology.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
• Children and adolescents aged under 18 years.
• Clinically indicated venous haemoglobin measurement as part of routine care.
• Written informed consent from at least one parent with parental responsibility.
• Additional age-appropriate information provided to children and adolescents capable of understanding the study.
Exclusion criteria:
• Patients aged over 18 years.
• Refusal to participate or absence of informed consent.
• Insufficient German language proficiency of the parents to provide informed consent.
• Patients for whom parental responsibility is held by a guardian, court-appointed custodian, youth welfare authority or another legal representative rather than by their parents.
